## mcrl metric get

Get a metric's time series.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl metric get (--host <host> | --service <service>) --name <metric> [flags]

Get a host or service metric's time series as [{"time", "value"}, ...].

Over a range of a day or longer, the API returns values aggregated over
coarser intervals instead of the raw one-minute points.

--since and --until accept "now", durations ago ("1h", "7d"), relative
times ("-30m"), RFC 3339, "2026-11-06 10:00" (local time) and epoch
seconds ("@1762390800").

API: GET /api/v0/hosts/<id>/metrics, GET /api/v0/services/<name>/metrics
API key permission: Read

Examples:
  mcrl metric get --host web-1 --name loadavg5
  mcrl metric get --service web --name response_time --since 6h --jq 'map(.value) | add / length'

Flags:
      --host string      host (ID, name or cid:<custom identifier>)
      --name string      metric name, e.g. loadavg5 (required)
      --service string   service name
      --since string     start of the time range (default "1h")
      --until string     end of the time range (default "now")
```

## mcrl metric graph-def create

Create or replace graph definitions of custom host metrics.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl metric graph-def create -f <file> [flags]

Create or replace graph definitions of custom host metrics, from a JSON or
YAML file in the API's format: an array of graph definitions, or one.

A graph definition sets how the custom metrics whose names start with its
name ("custom.<...>", where "*" and "#" are wildcards) are drawn: the
graph's display name, unit, and each metric's display name and stacking.
The API has no way to read graph definitions back, so the output is the
API's response ({"success": true}).

API: POST /api/v0/graph-defs/create
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl metric graph-def create -f graph-defs.yaml
  echo '{"name": "custom.queue", "unit": "integer", "metrics": [{"name": "custom.queue.length"}]}' | mcrl metric graph-def create -f -

Flags:
  -f, --file string   JSON or YAML file ("-" for stdin) (required)
```

## mcrl metric graph-def delete

Delete a graph definition.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl metric graph-def delete [--service <service>] <name> [flags]

Aliases:
  delete, rm

Delete the graph definition of custom host metrics with the name, or with
--service the graph definition of service metrics. The graph comes back
when metrics it covers are posted again. The output is the API's response
({"success": true}).

API: DELETE /api/v0/graph-defs, DELETE /api/v0/services/<name>/graph-defs/<graph>
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl metric graph-def delete custom.queue
  mcrl metric graph-def delete --service web 'custom.signups.*' --yes

Flags:
      --service string   delete a graph definition of this service's metrics
```

## mcrl metric latest

Get the latest values of host metrics.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl metric latest --host <host>... --name <metric>... [flags]

Get the latest values of host metrics.

The output is the API's {"<hostId>": {"<metric>": {"time", "value"}}} object.

API: GET /api/v0/tsdb/latest
API key permission: Read

Examples:
  mcrl metric latest --host web-1 --host web-2 --name loadavg5 --name memory.used
  mcrl metric latest --host web-1 --name loadavg5 --jq '.[].loadavg5.value'

Flags:
      --host stringArray   host (repeatable, required)
      --name stringArray   metric name (repeatable, required)
```

## mcrl metric names

List the metric names of a host or service.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl metric names (--host <host> | --service <service>) [flags]

List the metric names of a host or service.

API: GET /api/v0/hosts/<id>/metric-names, GET /api/v0/services/<name>/metric-names
API key permission: Read

Examples:
```

## mcrl metric post

Post metric values.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl metric post (--host <host> | --service <service>) (<name>=<value>[@<time>]... | -) [flags]

Post host or service metric values.

Values are given as name=value[@time] arguments, or with "-" read from stdin
in the plugin format "name<TAB>value<TAB>epoch" (one per line; any
whitespace separates the fields), or as a JSON array in the API's format.
The time defaults to now.

The API silently drops values older than 24 hours; mcrl warns about them.
Host metric names conventionally start with "custom.".

API: POST /api/v0/tsdb, POST /api/v0/services/<name>/tsdb
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl metric post --host web-1 custom.queue.length=42
  mcrl metric post --service web custom.signups=12@1762390800 custom.logins=340
  ./my-plugin.sh | mcrl metric post --host "$(hostname)" -

Flags:
      --host string      host (ID, name or cid:<custom identifier>)
      --service string   service name
```
